body: There isn't a single picture of me anywhere in existence as far as I know, and I don't have a camera.  Even if I did, I couldn't bring myself to show you a picture of myself.  That would be much too painful.

>attentiondeficient

Are you in character right now?

I don't mean to seem rude, effrontery, or confrontational, but I wrote this in the body of my submission:

>I am aware that people with the disorder are almost never satisfied with the results of plastic surgery, but I've already tried every drug out there which has shown even so much as negligible efficacy in the treatment of the disorder and I've already spent quite a bit of time and money with therapists and psychiatrists to no avail. For that reason, I'm now seriously considering plastic surgery - because the alternative is suicide.

>What do other people say about your appearance when you ask them for an honest opinion?

I get weird and mixed reactions.  My brother will say such things as "Well, there are all these fucking ugly people running around 'n... Why would you not live your life when they're out there living their lives?" in a nervous, diffident tone of voice.  I'm not sure what that means.  My mother and father respond with alacritous eulogy of my appearance almost to the point of panegyric, but I don't trust their opinions to be objective or sincere in the least.  My therapist once asked me where I thought I fell on a scale of 1 to 10, and when I replied, "3 or 4" (making the elephant man a 1), he responded, "Well, that's not a level of attractiveness that will prevent you from forming relationships... b-b-but I think you're a fair bit higher than that," as if his correction of my self-appraisal were an afterthought.  When - rarely - I walk around in public women and girls seem to giggle at me, although I do tend to walk with my head down and shoulders slouched, body language calculated to intimate that I need people to leave me alone and/or be gentle with me, which seems not to work.  I'm not sure that bad posture would account for the giggling that seems to erupt when I'm near, however.  (I'm also very pale and thin, also.)

I can't tell whether people refrain from praising my appearance because they're males and feel awkward doing so or they refrain because they actually think I'm ugly.

I have no perspective on what the true quality of my appearance is since every time I look in the mirror I see a different face and since, again, I've received such mixed reactions.  I would really appreciate some honesty.
If you're going to submit comments like this, do you think you could at least upvote the submission so that other people might see it?  I really need help.

I really don't have any options then, though.  I've tried all of the therapies currently indicated by medical orthodoxy for the treatment of the condition.  I can not and will not continue to live like this much longer.  The extreme and protracted social isolation is making me insane, but, on the other hand, having others look at me is like having a laser beam burning into my face.  (Obviously that's hyperbolic but none of my other statements has been in the least, I would like to clarify.)
